newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares end slightly higher in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares end slightly higher in dull trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly higher on Sunday in dull trading as investors remained on the sidelines, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares rose 0.73 percent, or 1.88 points, to 259.77 on low all-share turnover of 91 million shekels against 93 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.37 percent higher at 266.39.

"The market is weak and activity is tepid. The whole market is in a holding pattern as investors wait to see what will happen with the government. It's clear that Netanyahu cannot function this way," said Zvi Hoffman of Meitav Investments and Securities.
"Options speculators used the opportunity of (today's) low volume. They were the most active players in the market," Hoffman said.

At least eight legislators, irate over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's decision to hand over more occupied West Bank lands to Palestinian rule, have threatened to bolt the ruling coalition that commands 66 seats in the 120-member parliament.
The threat follows a narrow cabinet vote on Friday to hand over another nine percent of the occupied West Bank to full Palestinian rule.
Other traders said political events had no impact on trading.

"The government is stable and Netanyahu will remain in power. The market made a very big move and now it is looking for the appropriate level to consolidate," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities.

He said sentiment continues to be very positive, despite the profit-taking of the last few weeks. "Investors are simply waiting for the release of the February consumer price index (CPI) on Friday," Nahum said.

Analysts have been forecasting a relatively high CPI because of the weakening Israeli currency. Hoffman said that if the CPI figure were higher than one percent the central bank would leave interest rates unchanged, which would have a negative impact on the market.
Hoffman said it is difficult to discern the market's direction.
"The recent rise of the bond market and the positive earnings reports published so far are very encouraging, but we are still waiting for the political uncertainty to fade away," he said.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which rose 2.25 percent to 21,508 agorot on turnover of 5.0 million shekels; Israel Chemicals, which gained 1.0 percent to 402 agorot on turnover of 4.3 million shekel; and Bank Leumi, which rose 0.5 percent to 572 agorot on volume of 3.5 million shekels.
